comparedAgainst: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/hash-table-data-structure/ -- a dense, ad-supported reference page with no evident dark-mode support and no per-topic diagrams tailored to a chained-vs-open-addressing comparison; this article's two purpose-drawn, dual-themed SVG figures and 390px-tuned typography clear it easily on the design/UX axis.

https://www.tutorialsteacher.com/csharp/csharp-dictionary -- a plain C#-Dictionary tutorial with no figures, no dark theme and no phone-specific layout handling at all; this article's collapsible exercises, faded scroll cues and themed code panels are a clear step up.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.dictionary-2 -- reference-style API docs: functional and responsive but no diagrams, no worked examples, no exercises; not built to teach the buckets/entries layout the way this article's Figure 2 does.
justification: Real numbers from the serial `verify-page.mjs --drafts` run: Lighthouse 91/100/100/100 (all four categories clear the round's 90 floor), zero console errors, zero broken links, mobileOverflowPx 0. Both hand-written SVG diagrams (Figure 1: chaining-vs-open-addressing collision resolution; Figure 2: buckets[]/entries[] parallel-array layout) stay fully legible with correctly themed strokes and text at 390px in both light and dark screenshots, with every label readable without zooming. Heading hierarchy is clean: exactly one h1, h2 sections match the 'On this page' TOC one-for-one, and the one h3 ('Building HashMap<K,V>: real chaining, not pseudocode') is correctly nested under its parent h2 ('Collisions: chaining or open addressing') in both the page and the TOC. All four exercises collapse their solutions behind a working `<details><summary>Show solution</summary>` toggle, confirmed in mobile screenshots. Code/prose rhythm is otherwise good — worked example, then prose that explains the exact lines, repeated through nine sections — though several code blocks necessarily re-paste the full `HashMap<TKey,TValue>` class verbatim (required for each snippet to compile and run standalone under `run-code.mjs`), which makes for a long scroll-only-code stretch on mobile in the load-factor and worst-case sections; this is a site-wide convention, not a defect specific to this article, so it is not scored as an issue. The one real, article-level defect: the final comparison table ('Choosing chaining, open addressing, or Dictionary<TKey,TValue>', two columns, Situation/Use) loses its entire second column on mobile in both themes. I verified this is not the page-overflow bug a prior (unsaved) run may have meant — mobileOverflowPx is 0, and pixel-cropping the table's right edge at 4x zoom (light and dark) confirms the site's `.fade-r` mask-image gradient genuinely renders as a soft fade, not a hard clip. The real problem is upstream of that cue: the 'Situation' column's longest cell (46 characters, 'Key might otherwise be mutated after insertion') alone renders close to the full 390px viewport width, and the 'Use' column's longest cell (141 characters, a full sentence) trips `sizeTableColumns()`'s data-col='l' bucket (22rem/352px min-width) — so zero characters of 'Use' are visible without scrolling, not even a sliver, and there is no dedicated per-cell scroll indicator beyond the table's shared edge fade. This matters because at least one recommendation is stated only in that hidden column and nowhere else in the article body: 'Override GetHashCode/Equals together, from immutable state, or use a record.' Given most readers arrive on a phone (WRITER_GUIDE.md's own framing) and the guide explicitly warns that 'four columns of sentences will put half the table off-screen' and to 'keep cells to a phrase rather than a sentence,' this table's Use column (full sentences, up to 141 characters) is a direct instance of the pattern the guide tells writers to avoid, not a shell/component bug. It is writer-fixable: shorten Use cells to phrases (e.g. 'chaining over two arrays, O(1) expected', 'GetHashCode/Equals together, or a record', 'key on an immutable id') so both columns fit near 390px, or convert the table to a short list per the guide's own fallback suggestion.
